column5: Comment Text
Sorry to ask but how do we know the money is actually going to her treatment? I see so many of these campaigns lately and it's hard to know what to believe anymore..
i donated $25 and went into the page, they have updates with the MRI results and a detailed cost breakdown. felt pretty legit compared to other campaigns i've seen
i had doubts at first too but she's a patient at Mass General in Boston, the docs are real. i gave $15
I lost a close friend to a brain tumor. Back then these new treatments didn't exist. I really hope Emily makes it. Donated a small amount, if everyone chips in a little we'll get there
strength to you.. i know how hard it is. we also lost a family member to the same thing. at least now there's some hope with these new therapies
Does anyone know if dendritic cell immunotherapy actually works for GBM? I asked a friend who's a neurosurgeon and he said it's a really promising treatment, especially for glioblastoma
yeah there's a study in Nature Communications showing a 68% increase in survival. the problem is no US insurance covers it, that's why she needs the campaign
my dad's oncologist explained to us that dendritic cell vaccines are the most innovative thing out there right now but because of FDA red tape it'll take years to get approved here. it's shameful..
I shared this in a group but they took my post down, said no fundraising links allowed. If you can please share this post directly, it reaches more people that way
21 years old and a pre-med student.. it's just so unfair. donated what i could
that's what hit me hardest too. she wanted to be a doctor and now she's the one fighting for her life. life is cruel sometimes..
Donation made. Stay strong Emily 🙏
In a country with the best hospitals in the world we can't cover treatment for a 21-year-old girl. Shame on the system. I donated $50, it's the least I can do.
guys please share too, just hitting like isn't enough
Keep fighting Emily! From Chicago
Can someone explain to me why this treatment isn't covered? Ok they say it's "experimental" but if it saves lives why don't they include it? Bureaucracy is literally killing people
because FDA approval takes years and Emily doesn't have that time. that's what's tragic about it
How much have they raised so far? I went on the page and it says over $56,000 out of a $150,000 goal. If we all give a little it can be done
I was studying biology at her age, hoping to go into medicine. I can't imagine what she's going through. Her line "every donation isn't just money, it's time" broke my heart
done ✅ shared and donated
As the mom of a daughter the same age these stories destroy us. My husband and I both donated. From the bottom of my heart I hope everything goes well for her
I had my doubts at first but I went on the page and saw the updates, the MRIs, all documented. It's not like other campaigns where you only see a few sentences. I gave $20.

We're Emily's classmates in the pre-med program at Boston University. The whole program has mobilized, our Pre-Med Student Association is the biggest top donor. Anyone who can please help, even $5 makes a difference
If you can't help financially at least share. 1 share can reach someone who can
I'm crying 😢 21 years old oh my God.. Donation made
